designs.understanding: Six business dimensions (stage, sector, BOM category, entry mode, registration subtype, idea domain/idea type) have no owner. Each module spells its own values and its own substring cues: elicitation Sector has 12 coarse values (agri, health, it_services, finance...), the ecosystem taxonomy (backend/app/ecosystem/taxonomy.py SECTORS) has 20 ids (agritech, healthtech, saas, food, edtech, consumer...), the registry has 12 StartupTN categories, readiness.py:22 knows launched/scaling while the frontend and answers._STAGE_WORDS say revenue/growth, investors.py:131 maps rounds (pre_seed, seed...) straight onto founder stages, models/enums.py and slots.py define two EntryMode enums, and the stage slot has no enum at all (slots.py stage Slot has kind 'enum' but no enum=). Because Python string comparison against an unknown spelling is just False, every boundary crossing fails silently (revenue founders score 0, K_DOMAIN misses healthtech, PMFME routing depends on which vocabulary filled 'sector'). The domain is resolved twice (registry.detect_domain vs scan._local word overlap) and 'is this health' is decided three times (vote.idea_type, novelty._is_health, council evidence). The root cause is the absence of one importable vocabulary module with explicit, total mappings and a test that makes an unmapped value an error instead of a False.

flags_disputed.note: Holds. D5 as written would drop food/education/retail; the ecosystem 20-sector list already covers them (food, edtech, consumer, manufacturing), so the design uses it as the canonical second level rather than inventing a new list.

Holds; also note answers._STAGE_WORDS already produces 'revenue'/'growth', so the conversation itself writes values readiness cannot read. Investor 'seed/series_a' are funding rounds, a different dimension from product stage; the design keeps them separate with an explicit round->stage table instead of merging the words.

approaches.name: Canonical vocabulary module (StrEnums + explicit mapping tables + AST literal-ban test)
approaches.how: One module app/core/vocab.py owns Stage, SectorId (20 ids, two-level with StartupTN category), BomCategory, EntryMode, RegSubtype, IdeaType. Every other spelling is reached only through a total mapping function (from_elicitation, from_registry_category, investor_round_to_stages). A unit test walks the AST of listed modules and fails on string literals equal to any vocabulary value used in comparisons; a second test asserts every mapping is total over its enum.
approaches.basis: Python Enum/StrEnum + Pydantic native enum validation; the same pattern 4.1.2 plans for sectors; zero dependencies.
approaches.advantages: Silent False becomes an AttributeError/ValidationError or a failing test; one place to add a sector; works offline; Pydantic validates API inputs for free.
approaches.drawbacks: Touches many modules at once; stored sessions with old spellings need an alias upgrade on load.

approaches.name: Boundary normalisers only (normalise_sector/normalise_stage at API, plan facts, vote)
approaches.how: Keep each module's own strings; add normalise_* functions where data crosses a boundary.
approaches.drawbacks: Internal literals (K_DOMAIN, _scheme_rules, idea_type) keep drifting; every new consumer must remember to normalise; nothing fails when it forgets.

approaches.name: Shared JSON Schema / YAML vocabulary file read by Python and TypeScript
approaches.how: vocab.yaml lists values and aliases; Python and TS load it at runtime or codegen.
approaches.basis: Language-neutral data file; used by i18n-style projects.
approaches.advantages: One file for both stacks; editable by non-coders.
approaches.drawbacks: A second schema system beside Pydantic; runtime loading loses static typing and IDE checks; still needs the same mapping logic.

approaches.name: OpenAPI-generated TypeScript types (openapi-typescript) from backend enums
approaches.how: Backend enums appear in the OpenAPI schema; openapi-typescript generates TS types in the frontend build.
approaches.basis: Popular, maintained npm tool; pairs with 5.3.4 OpenAPI export.
approaches.advantages: Frontend can never drift from backend for any enum exposed by a route.
approaches.drawbacks: Only covers frontend<->backend; enums not used in a route body are absent; adds an npm devDependency and an export step; does nothing for the Python-internal drift that causes most symptoms.

approaches.name: Learned or fuzzy classification (rapidfuzz / scikit-learn) of free text into the vocabulary
approaches.how: Map any free string or idea text to the nearest canonical value by similarity or a trained classifier.
approaches.basis: rapidfuzz is mature; sklearn is standard.
approaches.drawbacks: Silent wrong matches on short words ('smart'), no labelled data for a classifier, not explainable to founders, contradicts 'code decides' with a reviewed table.

designs.chosen: Canonical vocabulary module with explicit total mappings, a literal-ban test and a tiny in-repo TS generator (approach 1, with the frontend half of approach 4 done by a 40-line script instead of openapi-typescript)
designs.why_chosen: It fixes the cause, not the symptom: a value can only be produced by a member of an enum, and every foreign spelling (registry category, ecosystem id, investor round, old stored session) passes through one named, tested mapping. It costs no dependency, works offline, and gives T03 (typed slots), T04 (FounderFacts), T05 (consumer lists) and T06 (lever patches) the types they need. The two-level sector (StartupTN category on top for public labels, ecosystem sector id as the required join key) keeps every existing consumer target (PMFME on food, K_DOMAIN food/manufacturing, panel food row) instead of losing them as a 12-category list would. A small Python script that writes frontend/src/generated/vocab.ts (and a CI drift check) gives the frontend the same guarantee as openapi-typescript for these few enums without an npm dependency or a full OpenAPI export.

not_chosen.name: Boundary normalisers only
not_chosen.reason: Leaves internal literals in K_DOMAIN, _scheme_rules, idea_type and readiness that drift again; nothing fails when a new consumer forgets to normalise.

not_chosen.name: Shared JSON Schema / YAML vocabulary file
not_chosen.reason: Duplicates Pydantic with a second schema system and loses static typing; the mapping logic still has to live in Python.

not_chosen.name: openapi-typescript
not_chosen.reason: Only covers the frontend boundary and adds an npm dependency plus an OpenAPI export step; the in-repo generator covers the same enums now and can be swapped for openapi-typescript when 5.3.4 lands.

not_chosen.name: Fuzzy / learned classification
not_chosen.reason: Produces silent wrong matches (the exact bug being fixed), needs labelled data that does not exist, and is not explainable; contradicts decision 0002 (code decides from reviewed tables).

design.algorithm: Mapping is table lookup, never substring. Stage comparison uses Stage.ORDER index (for 'stage floor' and investor ranges). Sector cue matching: compile each SectorId's cue words as \b...\b regexes once; hits ordered by first position in the text, ties by table order. design.interfaces: T03 uses vocab enums as the slot types and coerce() targets and gets REG_FACTS/entry-mode mapping as PROFILE facts. T04 FounderFacts uses Stage, SectorId, RegSubtype/entity. Funding (readiness, investors, investor_match), cohort router (sector: SectorId instead of ^[a-z_]+$), planner (plan.py facts, roadmap.K_DOMAIN as a set of SectorId, registry._scheme_rules comparing SectorId/StartupTNCategory), b2b, council vote, novelty all import from app/core/vocab.py.

design.offline: Entirely deterministic tables; no model or network. The optional model path (note_fact) receives the enum lists in the tool schema, but the server still validates.

designs.understanding: Reference data (registry cards, packs, regulatory items, scheme catalogue, translations, intake and investor signals, OpenAlex signals) is loaded as plain dicts with, at best, one file-level date. There is no per-item provenance record (source, checked_on, review state, reviewer), and the code never reads the review flags that do exist (registry review=draft on 190/240 cards; translations reviewed=false on all 38), so unreviewed drafts are stated as facts. Absence of district data reads as a weak fit because registry.fit returns 1 for any unknown district. The harvest scripts rewrite files from scratch so one failed fetch erases good records, the loader silently lets a later batch overwrite an id (and sorts batch10 before batch2), and the weekly workflow is fragile: PRs made with GITHUB_TOKEN never run ci.yml, one failing step discards the others, dated branches pile up, and the signals job refetches settled years. The root cause is that provenance and freshness are not part of the data model, so no runtime rule, test or workflow can act on them.

design.components: 1) app/core/provenance.py: Review enum (base, draft, approved), Provenance model {source: str|None, checked_on: date|None, review: Review, reviewed_by: str|None, reviewed_on: date|None, checklist: dict[str,bool]|None} with a validator: approved requires reviewed_by, reviewed_on and every checklist item from the batch _meta. 2) app/core/freshness.py: MAX_AGE = {intake: 14d, investor_signals: 30d, scheme_status: 30d, pack_prices: 180d, regulatory: 180d, signals: 365d}; status(dataset, checked_on, today) -> fresh|stale|unknown; label() gives 'not re-checked since <date>' or 'date not recorded'. ecosystem/intake.py and ecosystem/match.reachability use it (investor open_call/pitch_route older than 30d scores like 'not checked' and is labelled). 3) Registry: load() raises DuplicateId naming both files; batches sorted by numeric _meta.batch; cards parsed with provenance; registry.fit(d, district) returns None for districts outside COVERED_DISTRICTS, and callers say 'Vanigam has no district data for Salem yet' instead of a weak fit; a demand counter (district asked, not covered) is logged for curation (5.6). 4) Review state reaches speech: tools._domain_row/_roadmap carry review and checked_on; the offline wording and the model prompt mark draft facts 'from a draft card, not yet checked'; the fact-check treats them as backed but labelled. 5) Translations: phrasebook.translation(text, lang) returns only reviewed entries unless settings.allow_unreviewed_translations (default False). 6) Packs and regulatory items: each price and each regulatory item has source and checked_on; costing shows 'prices as of <date>'. Scheme catalogue: per-scheme checked_on. 7) Harvest: scripts/_harvest.py merge(previous, fresh) keeps the last good record when a fetch is unreachable (record gets last_attempt and last_ok), plus a guard that fails the step if ok-count drops more than 50% versus the previous file; scripts write atomically (temp file then replace). 8) Signals: build_domain_signals.py incremental: per-domain checked_on; fetch domains missing or older than 180 days, oldest first, under a per-run request cap; write partial results after each domain; budget exhaustion exits 0 with a summary. 9) Workflows: .github/workflows/data-checks.yml (on: workflow_call) runs scripts/check_data.py and the data unit tests; ci.yml calls it; weekly-checks.yml runs each harvest step with continue-on-error, then calls the data checks, then peter-evans/create-pull-request (pinned by SHA) with fixed branch data/weekly-checks so one PR is kept current. A scheduled freshness job (weekly, same workflow) runs scripts/freshness_report.py and opens or updates one issue listing stale items; ci.yml has no clock-based gate.
design.data_model: Every curated item gains a 'provenance' object (or flat source/checked_on/review fields where an item already has some). Batch _meta keeps review_checklist; approved cards carry the checklist answers. Harvest records gain last_ok and last_attempt. signals.json entries gain checked_on.
design.algorithm: Freshness: age = today - checked_on; stale if age > MAX_AGE[dataset]; unknown if checked_on is None. Harvest merge: for each key, if fresh.status == 'unreachable' and previous exists, keep previous with last_attempt=now; ok_count guard compares counts of status in ('ok','open_call','pitch_route'). Signals: sort domains by (checked_on or epoch), take until cap.
design.interfaces: T04 uses freshness.status for scheme status checked_on and the catalogue loader. T01's card idea_type is a reviewed field. T05/T06 untouched. Agent tools (T03/T06 tool outputs) carry review and stale labels.
design.rollout: First the loader guards and runtime labels (no data change needed: missing dates read as 'date not recorded'). Then the workflow changes. Then backfill provenance per dataset from the sources already cited (never invented; unknown stays null). The approved-requires-reviewer validator is enforced from the start, which is safe because no card is approved today.
design.offline: All checks and labels are local file reads. The harvest and OpenAlex scripts are the only network users and run only in the weekly workflow; at runtime the app reads the last committed files.

designs.understanding: ElicitationSession.put (session.py:153-171) is the single merge point for every fact, but it is untyped and policy-free: it accepts any value for any slot, decides only by a bare confidence number with one exception (ANSWER over non-ANSWER), returns nothing, and discards the losing value. Entry points bypass the normaliser that already exists (answers.validate): engine.start writes profile values raw at 0.95 Source.PROFILE (engine.py:118-120), _note_fact writes model values raw, and the extractor at 0.90 can overwrite a 0.90 ANSWER given on an earlier turn. The result is untyped values crashing the planner (TypeError not caught by run_tool), non-enum strings that silently miss every literal comparison, extractions overriding direct answers, a tool that says 'recorded' when it was dropped, a browser profile shape (nested founder/startup) that matches no slot key, and two different 'known' thresholds (filled >= 0.5, selector TAU_FILL 0.60). Root cause: there is no typed fact contract (value type per slot, a source precedence table, an explicit outcome) and no mapping layer from external shapes (browser draft, server profile, entry subtype) onto slots.

design.components: 1) Slot table (slots.py) gains max_len for text/multi (e.g. 300 chars, 10 items) and uses T01 enums (SectorId, Stage). 2) answers.coerce(key, value) -> typed value | None: enum member or its value passes; known alias via vocab.upgrade_slot_value; str goes through validate(); int within bounds; list of short strings for multi; anything else None. 3) Source enum gains CHOSEN (founder picked a lever or card) and NOTED (model note_fact; previously EXTRACTED). RANK = {CHOSEN: 4, ANSWER: 4, PROFILE: 3, DOCUMENT: 2, EXTRACTED: 1, NOTED: 1, DEFAULT: 0}. 4) put(key, value, confidence, source, *, answering=False) -> PutOutcome: reject if key unknown or coerce fails (outcome rejected, reason); if no existing -> stored; if new rank > existing rank -> stored; if equal rank and rank >= 3 -> later wins only when it is a direct answer to that slot's question or an explicit correction (answering=True), otherwise kept_existing + rival; if equal low rank: same value -> stored with max confidence; different value -> conflict: keep existing, add rival, cap confidence at TAU_ASK - 0.01 so the slot becomes askable; if new rank < existing rank -> kept_existing, and a differing value is added to rivals (no confidence change for rank >= 3 sources, so an offhand sentence never reopens a direct answer). 5) Confidence bands in one place (slots.py): TAU_KNOWN = 0.75, TAU_ASK = 0.50. KNOWN (>= 0.75, or rank >= 3): stated as fact, never asked. ASSUMED (0.50-0.75): counted filled for the stop rule, not asked, restated with 'I assumed'. UNKNOWN (< 0.50) or disputed: askable. session.filled and selector.candidates both import these. 6) ProfileIn (routers/ideation.py): allowlisted optional fields district, sector, stage, founder_years, founder_skills, owned_assets with max lengths; extra='forbid'. 7) elicitation/profile.py: profile_to_slots(source_dict, *, shape) -> (accepted: dict, ignored: list[key]) used by engine.start for the client ProfileIn, by the server mapper for a signed-in founder's profile row (models/startup.domain -> sector via vocab, stage via stage_from_any), and by T01's REG_FACTS (stage floor). Accepted values are put at 0.95 Source.PROFILE through put(); ignored keys are returned to the client in the start response as profile_ignored so the screen can say what will be asked. PROFILE_SLOTS gains stage. 8) Server preference: when the request is authenticated (3.1.2), the server loads the profile itself and ignores client profile values for the same keys. 9) Frontend agentClient.startSession sends an explicit allowlisted projection of the nested ProfileDraft (founder.district -> district, startup.stage -> stage, startup.domain -> sector); protected fields (caste, phone, date of birth) never leave the browser for this purpose. 10) tools.note_fact schema lists per-key enums generated from the slot table; _note_fact returns the PutOutcome (stored/kept_existing/conflict/rejected with reason) so the model is told the truth. 11) AgentSession.from_dict re-coerces stored slot values; values that fail are dropped with a log line (they will be asked).
design.data_model: SlotValue gains rivals: list[{value, source, confidence, turn}] (bounded to 3). PutOutcome = Enum(stored, kept_existing, conflict, rejected) returned with an optional reason string. AgentStartIn.profile: ProfileIn | None. Start response gains profile_ignored: list[str].
design.algorithm: Precedence by rank first, then the direct-answer rule, then confidence only within the lowest ranks; conflicts lower confidence below TAU_ASK so the selector asks; a founder ANSWER resolves the conflict and clears rivals.
design.interfaces: T01 provides enums and alias upgrade. T04 projects FounderFacts from typed slots (no string guessing). T05 uses the three bands and the disputed state (conflict -> candidate with a 'which is it' question). T06 writes lever patches with Source.CHOSEN, so later extraction cannot undo them. T07 untouched.
design.rollout: Ship coerce + precedence + outcome in one PR with tests from every flag probe; then ProfileIn and the mapper; then the frontend projection; then the server-profile path when 3.1.2 lands. from_dict re-coercion makes existing sessions safe on first load.
design.offline: All deterministic. The model path only adds note_fact calls, which go through the same put().

designs.understanding: The scheme engine is two-valued: rules._apply returns False when the field is missing (rules.py:48-49), and engine.check_eligibility has only eligible/ineligible buckets, so 'not known yet' is reported as 'not eligible' with a false reason. (IS_FALSE on a missing field even passes, since bool(None) is False, the opposite error.) The profile the rules read is an untyped dict (scheme_schemas founder/startup: dict[str, Any]); seed rules and catalogue 'inputs' use different names for the same fact (dpiit_recognized vs dpiit, incorporation_age_years vs age_years), state is a case-sensitive free string, and nothing projects conversation slots onto it. Scheme facts are flattened: the Scheme dataclass has no status (catalogue says sisfs closed, standup_india revamping), min/max_funding mean subsidy for one scheme and loan size for another, TANSEED is a GRANT so ranking calls it non-dilutive despite the 3% stake, and seed age bands contradict the catalogue (NEEDS 55 for special categories, UYEGP 35 general). Finally /talk's support_for picks schemes from the domain card's own fields, never the founder's, so the conversation and the Schemes screen disagree. Root cause: no three-valued logic, no typed FounderFacts contract, and scheme metadata that does not model status, money units or equity.

Reasons only from FALSE leaves; missing from UNKNOWN leaves. 2) schemes/profile.py: FounderFacts(BaseModel) with founder: {state: Literal['tamil_nadu', 'other'] normalised by validator, age: int|None, gender: Gender|None, caste_category: CasteCategory (general, bc, mbc, sc, st, ews, obc) | None, special_category: set[SpecialCategory] (women, ex_servicemen, differently_abled, transgender), first_graduate: bool|None, rural: bool|None, tn_residency_years: int|None} and startup: {stage: Stage|None, sector: SectorId|None, district: str|None, entity_type: EntityType|None, dpiit: bool|None, startuptn_registered: bool|None, incorporation_age_years: float|None, annual_revenue: int|None, women_led: bool|None}. Sensitive founder fields are never projected from the conversation; they come only from the consented Schemes screen. 3) engine.py: buckets eligible, not_eligible (with reasons), needs_info (with missing field paths and a human question per field from a FIELD_QUESTIONS table). Soundness/Completeness properties restated for three values. 4) Scheme metadata: SchemeStatus enum (open, between_calls, revamping, closed) + status_note + checked_on joined from funding_catalogue.json by id at load (one status source); money fields project_min, project_max, benefit_max, benefit_rate (optional) replacing min/max_funding; dilutive: bool and equity_pct. Ranking: _funding_fit compares need against the project range and shows benefit separately; 'non-dilutive' only when not dilutive; closed/revamping/between_calls go to a 'not open now' group with the status note, never mixed with open ones. annotate.py places only open schemes on milestones and labels between_calls as 'next call expected'. 5) Seed corrections against the catalogue: NEEDS age 21-45 general, up to 55 for special categories; UYEGP 18-35 general, 18-45 special; TANSEED stage prototype/mvp, entity pvt_ltd/llp, dilutive with 3%. tests/unit/test_seed_matches_catalogue.py compares seed rule bounds with structured catalogue fields (age_general, age_special added for encoded schemes, cited). 6) /talk: tools._support_for(session) = registry.schemes_for(domain) as a relevance shortlist, then engine.check_eligibility(facts_from_session(slots), shortlist) and returns eligible / needs_info / not_eligible with reasons and status. registry._scheme_rules keeps relevance only. 7) Frontend Schemes.tsx: 'not yet incorporated' and 'no revenue yet' choices send null/false explicitly, state as a select, caste options include bc/mbc, special categories as checkboxes, rural checkbox; shows needs_info as 'Could qualify, tell us...', unmodelled_notes as 'Also check', and status badges.

designs.understanding: The interview has no single question policy. The budget unit is wrong: is_objective_clear stops at session.turn_no >= Q_MAX where turn_no = len(turns), so the opening pitch, each re-ask and each opinion request consume the 7-question budget, while the IDEA mode requires 9 slots. Dynamic questions (scan and panel) bypass the selector: step() asks a pending dynamic question before required slots, add_dynamic is first-come with a shared cap of 3 so scan points shut out the panel, the panel question offline is always the customer seat's (a duplicate of the beneficiary question), and their answers are stored in d['answer'] and never read. The WHY finger has no required slot so the five-finger rule checks four fingers; slot value is a static consumer count blind to what the session actually needs; restate() names only session.missing (which excludes skipped slots) and omits the planner's inputs (team_size, founder_years, time_horizon); CP-SAT is solved twice per turn and never differs from greedy. Root cause: there is no one policy that decides (a) what counts against the budget, (b) which candidate (slot or dynamic) is worth asking given what is still blocked downstream, and (c) what is restated as an assumption when it was not asked.

approaches.name: One QuestionPolicy in selector.py: unified candidate pool (slots + bound dynamic questions), questions-asked budget with must-ask/assumable tiers, dynamic value from blocked consumers, greedy lexicographic selection
approaches.how: Candidates are slots and dynamic questions; each has a value = static part + blocked-consumer term (how many scheme decisions / roadmap gates are UNKNOWN only because of it) and a class (must_ask, assumable, enriching, dynamic). Selection is lexicographic: must_ask first, then dynamic (quota-limited) and assumable by value, then enriching. Budget counts questions actually asked. Unasked assumable slots are restated with their declared default. CP-SAT runs only when a burden budget can bind.

approaches.advantages: Fixes the budget unit, the bypass, the dedupe and the restatement with one decider; testable as a pure function.
approaches.drawbacks: Touches selector, engine and council question handoff together.

designs.chosen: One QuestionPolicy: questions-asked budget, must-ask vs assumable required tiers with declared defaults, dynamic questions as bound, quota-limited selector candidates, blocked-consumer value term, greedy lexicographic selection with CP-SAT only when a burden budget binds
designs.why_chosen: Every question (slot, scan point, panel question) goes through one decider that sees the remaining budget and what is still blocked, so the budget means questions, required facts come first, the panel is not shut out, and nothing is asked twice. Splitting REQUIRED into must-ask (cannot be guessed: problem, solution, beneficiary, sector, product_form, stage, district) and assumable (capital_band, funding_route, which have safe defaults the planner already widens) makes the 7-question budget feasible without lengthening the interview, and the declared default is exactly what the restatement says it assumed. A sort is the exact form of a lexicographic policy and is ~1000x cheaper than the solver; the solver remains for a binding budget.

design.components: 1) Session counters: questions_asked (incremented in step() when it returns an ask for a slot or dynamic not asked before; a re-ask of the same question and an opinion turn do not count) and asked_keys. Q_MAX now limits questions_asked. 2) Slot table: Need gains ASSUMABLE (still required for the stop rule, but may be closed by its declared default when the budget runs out); Slot gains assume: value and assume_label (e.g. capital_band -> under_2L 'under Rs 2 lakh'; funding_route -> self 'your own funds') and restate: bool (True for every non-text slot whose consumers include roadmap or scheme). A test asserts the planner's defaults equal slot.assume. 3) Candidate = SlotCandidate | DynamicCandidate. DynamicCandidate {key, question, source: scan|panel, binds: slot key | risk id | 'notes', dup_slot: slot key | None}. A dynamic candidate is dropped when dup_slot or binds is already KNOWN. Quota: panel <= 2, scan <= 1, total <= 2 asked per session; a panel arrival replaces an unasked scan one. Dynamics are eligible only once must-ask slots are covered or the remaining budget exceeds remaining must-ask slots. 4) Value: question_value = static (existing W_REQUIRED, W_CLASSES, W_BURDEN) + W_BLOCKED * blocked(key, session), where blocked = number of scheme decisions currently UNKNOWN only because of this slot (from T04 unknown_inputs, non-sensitive fields only) + number of roadmap gates waiting on it (planner reports gate inputs). The static W_CONSUMERS * len(consumers) term is dropped. Sensitive slots are filtered by slot.sensitive (and SENSITIVE_DEFERRED) in candidates(). 5) Selection: sort by (class rank: must_ask=0, dynamic/assumable=1, enriching=2; then -value); CP-SAT path called only if burden_budget < horizon * max burden. select_next called once per step; is_objective_clear receives the plan. 6) Stop rule: stop when must-ask covered and (assumable covered or questions_asked >= Q_MAX) and fingers satisfied; WHY finger counts as covered by any of why_now, differentiation, motivation at band ASSUMED or better (extraction included), and an uncovered WHY never forces a question by itself; a panel or scan question bound to differentiation can cover it. 7) Dynamic answers: an answer to a question bound to a slot is put() as Source.ANSWER into that slot (T03); bound to a risk id it is stored in session.founder_notes with the risk id; otherwise founder_notes with 'notes'. founder_notes are passed to the council and planner and restated as 'You told me ...'. The offline 'Things to think through' list excludes any point that is queued or asked. 8) Panel question choice (vote.py): when no criterion spread > DISAGREE, ask from the seat that scored the weakest criterion; each seat question in rules.py is tagged with dup_slot (customer seat -> beneficiary); skip when that slot is KNOWN. 9) restate(): built from the slot table: core sentences as today; then 'I assumed: ...' for every restate slot whose band is ASSUMED or whose source is EXTRACTED/NOTED/DEFAULT (team size, experience, horizon, geo scope included); then 'You skipped X / I could not ask about Y; I will assume Z' for every required slot that is skipped, dropped or unasked, using slot.assume_label; gaps include skipped slots.
design.data_model: ElicitationSession gains questions_asked: int, founder_notes: list[{text, binds, source}], dynamic entries gain binds and dup_slot. Slot gains assume, assume_label, restate; Need gains ASSUMABLE. Selector constants: Q_MAX=7 (questions), DYN_QUOTA={'panel':2,'scan':1}, DYN_TOTAL=2, W_BLOCKED.
design.algorithm: Lexicographic greedy over the unified pool; blocked() is a cached count recomputed when slots change (scheme engine on facts_from_session is microseconds for 8-46 schemes).
design.interfaces: Requires T03 (bands, put outcomes, disputed slots become candidates with a 'which is it' question). Uses T04 unknown_inputs for the blocked term. T06: dynamic questions carry the research_key/council_key they came from and are dropped if the key changes. Council (vote.py, rules.py) emits question with dup_slot and binds.

designs.understanding: idea_version (ideation.py:136-142) hashes the text of every core slot, so filling sector or product_form produces a new version (4 versions in a 7-turn interview), while choosing a lever (which carries no slot patch; novelty.py _levers returns only kind/text/because) usually changes nothing. No artefact records what it was built from: jobs are keyed (session, kind) with reuse_done=True and write under LATEST (jobs.py:62-79), _absorb takes research only when s.scan is None, council results are applied if 'at' differs, s.roadmap/s.novelty/s.council are single unversioned fields, narration keys ('statement', 'lever:{i}', 'searching') are global and positional, the panel sees only levers[:4] in a fixed kind order and the prior-art seat endorses lever 0, and lever text is baked at search time. The ResultStore already has an idea_version parameter that the board ignores. Root cause: there is no declared dependency key per artefact (which inputs each result depends on), so nothing can decide whether a result is current, reusable or stale.

approaches.name: Declared input keys per artefact kind (dependency hashing, like a build system) + structured levers with stable ids and slot patches
approaches.how: A table KEY_INPUTS declares, per artefact kind, which inputs it reads: research -> public search terms (research/terms.py), elements, beneficiary, private, chosen-lever terms; council -> research_key + sector, product_form, stage, beneficiary, founder_notes; roadmap -> all planner facts + domain_id + council key. key(kind, session) = sha1 of those inputs; never None once there is text. Jobs, results, narration marks and session artefacts are tagged with the key they were built for; a mismatch means stale. Levers get id = hash(kind + facts) and patch {slot: value} applied as Source.CHOSEN.
approaches.basis: The memoisation/dependency-key pattern of build tools (Make, Bazel) and React's dependency arrays; uses the ResultStore interface that already exists.
approaches.advantages: Re-runs exactly when an input that matters changes; old results are reusable when an idea returns to a previous state; one check at absorb/narrate time.
approaches.drawbacks: Requires care that KEY_INPUTS stays complete (a missing input means a stale result is considered fresh); mitigated by tests.

approaches.drawbacks: Arbitrary N, delays real changes, lets a wrong early verdict stand; does not fix positional narration or lever patches.

Tagging every artefact with its key makes stale detection one comparison at absorb, narrate and apply time; it reuses the ResultStore keyed interface already in results.py and works with the in-process board (no Redis needed). Stable lever ids survive panel reordering and version changes, and late rendering lets wording follow the current sector without a new search.

designs.understanding: The store stack (MemoryStore, SqlStore, CachedStore over Redis) has no written contract. Lifetime is one constant IDLE_EXPIRY = 6 h (store.py:29) applied by every store's get(), while ElicitationSession.expired says 30 days (session.py:35, unused) and D4 decides 90 days in PostgreSQL with a 6 h Redis TTL. CachedStore applies _expired to Redis copies and refills Redis from the database with a fresh TTL but old updated_at, so with D4 implemented naively a resumed session 404s on the next turn. The Redis copy is written without a version guard and delete() drops the key before deleting the row, so an in-flight read resurrects a deleted session (erasure broken) or a slow read overwrites a newer copy (spurious 409). Durability is inferred from store.name == 'database' (broken by the '+redis' wrapper) and only sent at start; a DB outage after boot raises raw 500s and a DB that was down at boot pins the process to memory. Analytics (cohort programme) reuse the founder-resume read path, so sessions idle over 6 h vanish from aggregates and 500 documents are loaded one by one with a Redis fill each. Root cause: no explicit contract for durability, lifetime (idle expiry vs retention), version-guarded cache writes, outage behaviour, and a separate analytics read.

flags_disputed.note: Holds, but its recommendation (in-memory fallback for live DB sessions) conflicts with F-B2-012 (503 and no divergent copies). The design takes both halves: new conversations during an outage go to memory with saved=false (SYSTEM-DESIGN section 9), existing database conversations answer 503 with Retry-After rather than diverging.
Same defect as F-B3-004 and F-A2-003; resolved by one get_many method.

approaches.name: Explicit store contract: lifetime constants + durable flag + version-guarded cache (Lua CAS + tombstone) + analytics get_many + circuit-breaker routing store
approaches.how: SessionStore protocol declares durable, get (live), get_many (analytics, retention only, no cache fill), create/save/delete. One lifetime module: REDIS_TTL 6 h (cache only), RETENTION 90 d (all stores). CachedStore expires only by TTL, writes via a Lua script that sets the copy only if its version is newer and no tombstone exists, and delete writes a tombstone then deletes the row. A RoutingStore wraps the durable store with a small breaker: DB errors retried once then 503; new sessions while open go to MemoryStore with saved=false; a half-open probe restores the DB.
approaches.basis: redis-py (installed) supports EVAL; SQLAlchemy error classes; hand-rolled breaker ~40 lines.
approaches.advantages: Closes the resurrect and stale-overwrite races atomically, fixes resume-then-404, makes durability a declared property, honest outage behaviour, correct and cheap analytics.
approaches.drawbacks: More moving parts in store.py; Lua script must be tested with a Lua-capable fake or real Redis.

approaches.name: Drop the Redis copy entirely (database only)
approaches.how: Remove CachedStore; PostgreSQL is fast enough for one server.
approaches.advantages: Removes both races and the double clock.
approaches.drawbacks: Contradicts SYSTEM-DESIGN section 4.3 live-copy design and the future multi-worker step; does not fix outage, durability flag or analytics.

approaches.name: Write-only cache (fill Redis on save/create only, never on read) + reorder delete
approaches.how: Avoid read-fill races by never filling on read.
approaches.drawbacks: A concurrent save can still re-create a deleted copy; reorder narrows but does not close the window.

approaches.name: Redis WATCH/MULTI optimistic transactions
approaches.how: Guard writes with WATCH on the key.
approaches.drawbacks: Retry loops and more round trips than one EVAL; more code paths.

approaches.name: Library breaker/retry (pybreaker, aiobreaker, tenacity)
approaches.how: Use a library for outage handling.
approaches.advantages: Less custom code for the breaker.
approaches.drawbacks: New dependency for ~40 lines; the fallback routing still has to be written by hand.

approaches.name: Nightly analytics snapshot tables (5.5.5) instead of a get_many read
approaches.how: Rebuild aggregates nightly from the session table.
approaches.drawbacks: Blocked on 2.1.1/2.1.4; today's endpoint stays wrong; still needs a retention-based reader to build from.

designs.chosen: Explicit store contract: lifetime module (Redis TTL only for the copy, 90-day retention everywhere), durable flag, Lua compare-and-set cache writes with tombstones, get_many for analytics, and a RoutingStore with a hand-rolled breaker (retry once, 503 for existing DB sessions, memory for new ones, half-open probe)
designs.why_chosen: Each symptom is a missing clause of one contract, so writing the contract into the protocol and one lifetime module fixes them together and makes callers stop inferring behaviour from names. The Lua CAS + tombstone is the only cache option that closes both races atomically in one round trip with an installed library. The breaker gives section 9's promised degraded mode for new conversations without creating divergent copies of database sessions, and the half-open probe removes the sticky memory-at-boot state. get_many fixes analytics counts and cost now and is the clean interface 5.5.5 can replace later.

design.components: 1) agents/lifetime.py: REDIS_TTL = 6 h (cache copy only), RETENTION = 90 d (D4; applied by SqlStore and MemoryStore get), saved ideas kept until deleted (needs 3.1); kept_until(s, store) = updated_at + RETENTION if store.durable else 'until this server restarts'. ElicitationSession.IDLE_EXPIRY and .expired are removed (dead, contradictory). 2) SessionStore protocol: durable: bool; get(id) -> live session within retention; get_many(ids, *, consent_only=True) -> list (one SELECT ... WHERE session_id = ANY(:ids) AND last_active > now()-RETENTION AND cohort_consent, no Redis fill); create/save/delete. MemoryStore.durable=False, SqlStore.durable=True, CachedStore.durable=inner.durable, RoutingStore.durable_for(session). 3) CachedStore: no _expired on Redis copies (TTL only); get on miss reads inner and fills via CAS; save fills via CAS after inner.save; delete: SET tomb:{id} (TTL = REDIS_TTL) then inner.delete then DEL sess:{id}. CAS Lua: if EXISTS tomb:{id} return 0; local cur = GET sess:{id}; if cur and cjson.decode(cur).version >= ARGV.version return 0; SET sess:{id} ARGV.doc EX ttl; return 1. 4) RoutingStore(durable=CachedStore|SqlStore, memory=MemoryStore): create -> durable unless breaker open, then memory (session.home='memory'); get -> memory if the id is there, else durable; DB errors (sqlalchemy OperationalError, DBAPIError, OSError) retried once, then breaker opens for 30 s and the router answers 503 'This conversation can't be reached right now; try again in a minute' with Retry-After; half-open probe on the next call after 30 s; auto mode at boot uses the same breaker instead of a permanent choice. 5) Router: saved = store.durable_for(session) and kept_until returned by agent_start, agent_resume (snapshot) and each turn response; StoreUnavailable mapped to 503 in core/errors.py. Talk.tsx banner text derived from saved/kept_until. 6) routers/cohort.py uses store.get_many; response adds sessions_found and sessions_not_found (expired or unknown), and consent filtering happens before parsing.
design.data_model: agent_sessions table: add cohort_consent boolean column (Alembic migration, backfilled from data) and an index on last_active; AgentSession gains home: 'database'|'memory' (not persisted). No change to the JSON document otherwise.
design.algorithm: Breaker: closed -> on failure after one retry -> open (until t+30 s) -> half-open: one call allowed; success closes, failure re-opens. CAS by the monotonically increasing session version that save() already maintains.
design.interfaces: T06 artefact tags and T03 typed slots travel in the same document. Cohort aggregates (programme.py) unchanged apart from input source. 3.2.4 erasure uses delete() and benefits from the tombstone. 5.5.5 can replace get_many later.
design.rollout: 1) lifetime module + TTL-only cache + durable flag (fixes resume-then-404 and the banner); 2) CAS + tombstone; 3) get_many + migration; 4) RoutingStore/breaker + 503 mapping + runbook. Each step has a contract test run against MemoryStore, SqlStore (test DB) and CachedStore with a Lua-capable fake Redis.
design.offline: MemoryStore needs nothing; with no database the RoutingStore keeps new sessions in memory and says so (saved=false, kept until restart). Redis remains optional; every Redis error is swallowed as today.
